s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements due to deficiencies
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the natal cleft, buttocks, inguinal creases, and vulva
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
Purpuric macules present periorbitally, on the lips, inframammary folds, forearms, and thighs
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister lined by fibrin and chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
Scattered short eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple myeloma and biopsy findings showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining, which is characteristic of amyloid deposits

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has low serum zinc level and symptoms such as skin lesions and ulcers, which are consistent with zinc deficiency

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple myeloma and symptoms such as painful blisters and ulcers, which are consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus

shortlist.label: Linear IgA disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms such as skin lesions and ulcers, and biopsy findings showing subepidermal blister, which are consistent with linear IgA disease

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple myeloma and biopsy findings showing amyloid deposits, which is consistent with multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma, low serum zinc level, and biopsy findings of subepidermal blisters with apple-green birefringence on Congo red staining are consistent with multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis, which can cause skin lesions, macroglossia, and peripheral neuropathy

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: Too broad, as the patient has a specific type of amyloidosis associated with multiple myeloma

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
rejected.why: Although the patient has a low serum zinc level, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more consistent with amyloidosis

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not match paraneoplastic pemphigus, which typically involves autoantibodies against epithelial proteins

rejected.label: Linear IgA disease
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show linear IgA deposits, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with amyloidosis
